core_principles.text: Setting up in a half-kneeling position helps identify the proper stance length for your body before starting a set.
Keep feet hip-width to shoulder-width apart rather than placing one foot directly in front of the other.
Keep most of your body weight on the front foot and just enough on the rear leg to assist with balance.

common_mistakes.text: Stepping too far forward or backward creates an excessively long stance where the rear knee does not bend enough.
Stepping one foot directly in front of the other creates a narrow, narrow-line stance like walking a tightrope.
Placing too much weight in the back foot reduces focus on the lead leg.

specific_findings.text: Proper stance length allows both knees to bend to or close to 90 degrees pain-free.
A weight distribution cue of 80 percent of body weight on the front foot and 20 percent on the back foot targets the front leg while preserving balance.

consequences.text: An excessively long stance increases pressure on the back knee because it does not bend as much, which over time can cause knee pain and discomfort.
Placing one foot directly in front of the other creates an unstable base that causes the lifter to wobble.
Placing too much weight in the back foot can irritate the back knee.
